previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a male with HLA-B27-positive ankylosing spondylitis, hypertension, asthma, obstructive sleep apnea, and obesity, was admitted for severe right sacroiliac joint and hip pain rated 10/10, limiting mobility and causing urinary accidents. He had self-initiated a prednisone taper and increased hydromorphone use at home without adequate relief. Labs showed elevated CRP indicating inflammation, but no infection. He was managed with IV pain control initially, transitioned to PCA, then to oral OxyContin and oxycodone. Rheumatology supported the steroid taper, and orthopedics ruled out hip effusion. Pain and mobility improved significantly by discharge. He was discharged home on a short prednisone taper, long-acting and breakthrough opioids, with follow-up planned in rheumatology and pain clinics. Concerns remain about untreated ankylosing spondylitis due to prior discontinuation of biologics over infection fears.
problems: Ankylosing spondylitis of multiple sites in spine
Long term (current) use of systemic steroids

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  CT C-SPINE W/O CONTRAST Q311 CT SPINE

INDICATION:  History: ___ with ankylosing spondylitis with severe worsening of
pain and history of chronic steroid use.  Question of fracture.

TECHNIQUE:  Non-contrast helical multidetector CT of the cervical spine was
performed. Soft tissue and bone algorithm images were generated.  Coronal and
sagittal reformations were then constructed.

DOSE:  Acquisition sequence:
   1) Spiral Acquisition 5.5 s, 21.5 cm; CTDIvol = 22.6 mGy (Body) DLP = 487.6
mGy-cm.
   2) Sequenced Acquisition 1.0 s, 4.0 cm; CTDIvol = 15.0 mGy (Body) DLP =
60.0 mGy-cm.
 Total DLP (Body) = 548 mGy-cm.

COMPARISON:  CT cervical spine from ___

FINDINGS: 

Extensive soft tissue attenuation artifact secondary to the patient's body
habitus, as well as slight motion artifact, substantially limit evaluation of
osseous detail.

Alignment is normal.  Vertebral body heights are unchanged compared to
___.  Evaluation for nondisplaced fractures is substantially
limited; no definite displaced fracture is identified.  There is no evidence
for prevertebral edema.  There is no evidence for bridging enthesophytes. 
Evaluation of spinal canal detail is markedly limited.  No high-grade neural
foraminal narrowing is seen, though mild neural foraminal narrowing by
uncovertebral osteophytes may be present at several levels.

This exam is not technically optimized for evaluation of the included brain
parenchyma.  No gross abnormality is seen on limited assessment.  There is a
mucous retention cyst along the floor of the partially visualized right
maxillary sinus.  Partially visualized left maxillary sinus, and partially
visualized bilateral mastoid air cells, are clear.

No enlarged cervical lymph nodes are seen.  The thyroid is grossly
unremarkable.  Visualized lung apices are clear.

IMPRESSION:


1. This exam is substantially limited technically due to the patient's body
habitus.
2. Preserved alignment.  No change in vertebral body heights.  Evaluation for
nondisplaced fractures is markedly limited, though no clear evidence for a
fracture is seen.
